variants.headline: Party leader faces a challenge
variants.sub: A challenge to a party leader has opened in the colony.
variants.body:
A party's leader is being challenged in {colony}. The challenge places authority within the organisation in question, without deciding who should exercise it. Readers assessing {target} should distinguish the opening of a contest from an outcome that has not been established by this report.

The gazette notes the challenge as an internal political development. It records neither a change of leader nor the result of any contest. A reliable account should retain that distinction, particularly where a challenge encourages speculation about outcomes before the organisation has an established decision to report.

We take a favourable view of {target}. A leadership challenge does not make hostile interpretations correct, and a political position deserves support where the case against it rests on assumption. Care in the public record is part of responsible administration.

variants.headline: Leadership becomes a contested question
variants.sub: The leadership of a political party is under challenge.
variants.body:
The right to lead a party is being contested. That is the political development, rather than proof of an eventual removal or victory. An examination of {target} should begin with the challenge itself and leave the candidates' unreported programmes outside the factual account.

The gazette notes the challenge as an internal political development. It records neither a change of leader nor the result of any contest. variants.headline: A challenge inside the party
variants.sub: A party's leader is being challenged in {colony}.
variants.body:
Leadership can appear settled until it becomes a question again. A party leader now faces a challenge in {colony}. For {target}, the relevant issue is the exercise and scrutiny of political authority, not an imagined story about who has already secured the organisation's support.
